name: Alfred Hitchcock
signature: The master of suspense, who planned his films shot by shot and made the audience complicit in looking.
description: An English director who became Hollywood's most recognisable name. He storyboarded in detail and built scenes on what the viewer knows and the character does not, usually from a single character's point of view.

name: Orson Welles
signature: Reinvented film language at 25 with deep focus, long takes and a fractured story, then spent his career fighting for money and final cut.
description: A theatre and radio prodigy given unprecedented control over his first film. After Citizen Kane he worked mostly outside the studios, shooting in fragments across Europe whenever money allowed.

name: John Ford
signature: Turned Monument Valley into the landscape of American myth and framed people against doorways and horizons.
description: Directed over a hundred films from the silent era to the 1960s, above all westerns. His compositions are simple and monumental, and his subject is community: its rituals, its outsiders and its myths.

name: Douglas Sirk
signature: Hid sharp social criticism inside glossy Technicolor melodramas.
description: A German theatre director who fled the Nazis. His 1950s melodramas look like lush women's pictures and work as critiques of American conformity, which is why later directors keep returning to them.

name: Stanley Kubrick
signature: A perfectionist who reinvented a different genre with almost every film and controlled every detail.
description: An American who settled in England and made thirteen features across nearly every genre. He was known for exhaustive research, technical innovation and dozens of takes.

name: Akira Kurosawa
signature: Brought kinetic editing, weather and moral weight to the action film, and was remade around the world.
description: The Japanese director best known abroad, drawing on Shakespeare, Dostoevsky and the American western. He shot action with several cameras and long lenses and cut it with driving rhythm.

name: Yasujirō Ozu
signature: Filmed family life from a low, fixed camera and found the drama in what goes unsaid.
description: Spent his whole career at the Shochiku studio, refining one subject: the Japanese family as children marry and parents age. Over time he removed camera movement, fades and dissolves until only cuts and stillness remained.

name: Kenji Mizoguchi
signature: Told stories of women's suffering in long, flowing takes that keep a respectful distance.
description: Directed from the early 1920s until his death in 1956, and became known in the West only in his last years. His camera moves like a scroll painting unrolling, keeping its distance from suffering.

name: Ingmar Bergman
signature: Turned the human face into a landscape and made doubt, faith and marriage his subjects.
description: A Swedish theatre director who wrote almost all his own films. With a small troupe of actors he examined faith, marriage, illness and artistic vanity, often on a bare island.

name: Carl Theodor Dreyer
signature: Stripped cinema down to faces, walls and silence in search of the spiritual.
description: A Danish director who made few films, years apart, each with a different style. All share a slow, stripped intensity and a focus on women persecuted for their faith or love.

name: Robert Bresson
signature: Rejected acting altogether: he called his performers models and drained their delivery of expression.
description: Developed a system he called the cinematograph, opposed to filmed theatre. He used non-professionals drilled to speak without inflection, and built scenes from fragments of gesture and sound.

name: Andrei Tarkovsky
signature: Called filmmaking sculpting in time and filled his long takes with water, fire and memory.
description: A Soviet director in constant conflict with the film authorities. His films move at the pace of contemplation, mixing colour and black and white, dream, memory and newsreel.

name: Sergei Eisenstein
signature: The theorist of montage, who believed meaning is created when two shots collide.
description: A Soviet theatre director and engineer who became cinema's first major theorist. He conceived films as arguments made by the collision of shots, and cast by physical type.

name: Dziga Vertov
signature: Rejected fiction entirely and used every trick of the camera to show life caught unawares.
description: Founder of the Kino-Eye group, he saw fiction film as a drug and the camera as a machine for seeing truthfully. His films are also catalogues of trick effects.

name: Fritz Lang
signature: Built worlds of fate, surveillance and crowds, first in Weimar Germany and then in American film noir.
description: The leading director of Weimar Germany, where he made monumental silent films and the first great sound thriller. In Hollywood after 1934 he turned his geometry and fatalism into film noir.

name: F. W. Murnau
signature: Freed the camera to move and told stories almost without intertitles.
description: A German director of the silent era who made the camera mobile and expressive. He went to Hollywood in 1926, made Sunrise for Fox, and died just before the premiere of his last film.

name: Jean Renoir
signature: A humanist who staged life in depth, so the frame feels open on all sides.
description: The son of the Impressionist painter. His 1930s films mix comedy and tragedy and let actors move freely through deep, open spaces; the New Wave critics called him the patron of their cinema.

name: Roberto Rossellini
signature: Took the camera into the ruined streets of postwar Italy and made a new realism out of necessity.
description: His war trilogy, shot in the rubble with whatever film stock could be found, launched neorealism. He then moved toward spare studies of marriage and belief, and finally to teaching history on television.

name: Federico Fellini
signature: Began in neorealism and ended in a circus of memory, dreams and spectacle that gave us the word Felliniesque.
description: A caricaturist and gag writer from Rimini who started in neorealism. From La Dolce Vita onward his films became autobiographical spectacles shot on huge sets.

name: Michelangelo Antonioni
signature: Made alienation visible through architecture, empty space and stories that refuse to resolve.
description: Began in neorealist documentary and turned to the emotional lives of the wealthy. His stories dissolve mid-way while the camera lingers on walls, streets and empty landscapes.

name: Jean-Luc Godard
signature: Broke every rule of film grammar and then spent sixty years asking what cinema is.
description: A Swiss-French critic who became the most radical of the New Wave directors. Each phase of his career, from pop collage to militant essay to video, reinvented how sound, image and text relate.

name: François Truffaut
signature: The warmest of the New Wave directors, who followed one character, Antoine Doinel, across twenty years.
description: A critic rescued from delinquency by André Bazin. His films are lyrical, literate and affectionate toward their characters, and often about children or obsessive love.

name: Agnès Varda
signature: Moved freely between fiction, documentary and self-portrait, with a curiosity that never dimmed.
description: A photographer who made her first film with no training. She called her method cinécriture, writing in film, and kept inventing forms into her nineties.

name: Alain Resnais
signature: Made time and memory the structure of his films, not just their subject.
description: Started with documentaries on art and the camps. His features, written by leading novelists, treat consciousness itself as the setting.

name: Luis Buñuel
signature: A lifelong surrealist who attacked church, bourgeoisie and good taste with a straight face.
description: A Spaniard who worked in France, Mexico and Spain. His plain, unshowy direction makes his attacks on religion, class and sexual hypocrisy all the more disconcerting.

name: Jean-Pierre Melville
signature: Remade the American gangster film as a cool, near-wordless ritual of hats, trench coats and codes of honour.
description: Took his pseudonym from his favourite American author and built his own studio. His gangster films strip the genre to gesture and code, and his independence showed the New Wave how to work.

name: Jacques Tati
signature: Built comedy out of sound, architecture and crowds, with almost no dialogue and no close-ups.
description: A music-hall mime who made only six features. His comedy is democratic: gags happen all over a wide frame, and the viewer has to find them.

name: Satyajit Ray
signature: Brought Indian cinema to the world with quiet, humane films rooted in Bengali life.
description: A Calcutta commercial artist who taught himself to direct. His films observe Bengali life with patience and economy, and he wrote, scored and designed them himself.

name: Sergio Leone
signature: Stretched the western into opera with extreme close-ups, long silences and Ennio Morricone's music.
description: A Roman who reinvented the American western in Spain with Italian money. He alternates huge landscapes with extreme close-ups and stretches time until a duel becomes a ceremony.

name: John Cassavetes
signature: The father of American independent film, who paid for raw, actor-driven dramas with his own acting fees.
description: A successful actor who financed his own films. He wrote full scripts and then let the actors find the scenes, keeping the camera on faces through long emotional confrontations.

name: Robert Altman
signature: Filled the frame and the soundtrack with people talking at once and let their stories overlap.
description: A television veteran who became the great satirist of 1970s America. He let large casts improvise, recorded them on multiple tracks and roamed among them with the zoom.

name: Martin Scorsese
signature: Combines restless camera movement, rock music and Catholic guilt in stories of men on the edge.
description: Grew up in New York's Little Italy and came out of NYU film school. His films study violent, guilt-ridden men with an encyclopaedic knowledge of film history behind every shot.

name: Terrence Malick
signature: Makes films like whispered prayers: natural light, a roaming camera and voice-over in place of plot.
description: Studied philosophy before making two films in the 1970s and then disappearing for twenty years. His later films are assembled in the edit from roaming footage and whispered voice-overs.

name: Steven Spielberg
signature: The most commercially successful director in history, with an instinct for staging, wonder and suspense.
description: The defining popular filmmaker of his era. He combines classical staging in long, moving takes with an instinct for awe and suspense, and has alternated entertainments with historical dramas.

name: David Lynch
signature: Found dread under the surface of small-town America and made dream logic feel like plot.
description: A painter who came to film through animation. His films mix small-town innocence with nightmare, and treat sound as seriously as image.

name: Werner Herzog
signature: Chases what he calls ecstatic truth, in jungles, deserts and extreme states of mind.
description: A self-taught Bavarian who has filmed on every continent. He treats documentary and fiction as the same pursuit, inventing and staging in search of what he calls ecstatic truth.

name: Rainer Werner Fassbinder
signature: Made over forty films in about fifteen years, turning Hollywood melodrama into a critique of West Germany.
description: The driving force of the New German Cinema. He worked at furious speed with a fixed troupe, applying the forms of Hollywood melodrama to stories of exploitation in West Germany.

name: Chantal Akerman
signature: Made time itself the drama, showing domestic routine at full length from a fixed, frontal camera.
description: A Belgian director who saw avant-garde film in New York at twenty-one. Her films combine its rigour with European narrative, and return constantly to rooms, routines and her mother.

name: Abbas Kiarostami
signature: Blurred the line between fiction and documentary until the distinction stopped mattering.
description: Started at an Iranian institute for children's education. His films are deceptively simple journeys that question what is staged and what is real, and leave their endings to the viewer.

name: Pedro Almodóvar
signature: Mixes melodrama, comedy and noir in saturated colour, with women at the centre.
description: Self-taught, he emerged from Madrid's post-Franco counterculture. His films combine outrageous plots with deep sympathy for their characters, most of them women.

name: Michael Haneke
signature: A cold, precise moralist who makes viewers ask why they are watching.
description: An Austrian who came from theatre and television. His films confront comfortable audiences with violence they would prefer not to consider, withholding explanation and release.

name: Béla Tarr
signature: Films a bleak, muddy Hungary in black and white, in takes that can last ten minutes.
description: A Hungarian director whose late films, made with the novelist László Krasznahorkai, follow people through mud, wind and rain in intricately choreographed long takes.

name: Aki Kaurismäki
signature: Tells stories of Finnish outsiders with minimal dialogue, stoic faces and old rock and roll.
description: Finland's best-known director. His working-class fables are laconic and funny, lit like 1950s melodramas and scored with rock and roll and tango.

name: Jim Jarmusch
signature: The cool minimalist of American independent film, drawn to drifters, strangers and dead time.
description: Came out of the New York downtown music scene. His films follow outsiders and foreigners drifting through America, and find comedy in pauses and misunderstandings.

name: Joel and Ethan Coen
signature: Brothers who write, direct and edit together, blending noir plots with deadpan absurdity.
description: Brothers from Minnesota who long shared writing, directing and editing. Their films are intricate genre exercises about foolish schemes, written in heightened regional speech.

name: Lars von Trier
signature: A provocateur who sets himself rules and restrictions, then breaks them.
description: A Danish director who announces rules and manifestos for each project. His films put suffering heroines through ordeals designed to test the audience as much as the characters.

name: Jean-Pierre and Luc Dardenne
signature: Brothers who follow working-class characters around Seraing, Belgium, with the camera at their shoulder.
description: Belgian brothers who made documentaries for twenty years. Their features follow one person through a moral crisis, with the camera inches from the back of the neck.

name: Claire Denis
signature: Tells stories through bodies, skin and rhythm more than through dialogue.
description: Grew up in French colonial Africa and assisted Wenders and Jarmusch. Her films are sensual and elliptical, more interested in bodies and rhythm than in explanation.

name: Wong Kar-wai
signature: Films longing and missed chances in smeared neon, slow motion and pop songs on repeat.
description: A Shanghai-born Hong Kong director. He builds his films in the editing room from months of improvised shooting, turning missed connections into pure mood.

name: Tsai Ming-liang
signature: Films loneliness in long, still takes of people waiting, eating and failing to meet.
description: A Malaysian-born director working in Taiwan, with the same lead actor in every film. His long static shots of lonely people have a deadpan humour.

name: Hirokazu Kore-eda
signature: A patient observer of families, chosen and biological, who began in documentary.
description: Began in television documentary. His family dramas are gentle on the surface and precise about loss, obligation and what makes people kin.

name: Apichatpong Weerasethakul
signature: Makes films in which ghosts, past lives and the jungle sit calmly alongside daily life.
description: A Thai director trained as an architect and in Chicago's art school. His films drift between the everyday and the supernatural without marking the border.

name: Kelly Reichardt
signature: Makes quiet, small-scale films about people on the margins of the American Northwest.
description: Works on small budgets in Oregon and edits her own films. Her stories of people with little money are patient, undramatic and attentive to landscape.

name: Quentin Tarantino
signature: A former video-store clerk who rebuilt genre cinema out of dialogue, shuffled chronology and quotation.
description: A film-obsessed former video-store clerk. He writes long, digressive dialogue scenes and assembles them out of order, borrowing freely from exploitation genres.

name: Wes Anderson
signature: Builds symmetrical, pastel dollhouse worlds populated by melancholy eccentrics.
description: A Texan whose style is instantly recognisable: symmetrical frames, lateral tracking shots, pastel palettes and deadpan delivery. Beneath the design are stories of grief and broken families.

name: Paul Thomas Anderson
signature: Moved from sprawling ensemble films to intense character studies, always with a restless camera.
description: Grew up in the San Fernando Valley, where several of his films are set. He began with sprawling ensembles and turned to intense portraits of obsessive men.

name: Bong Joon-ho
signature: Slides between comedy, horror and social critique inside tightly engineered genre films.
description: A South Korean director who storyboards every shot. His genre films swerve between comedy and horror and are built on the architecture of class.

name: Park Chan-wook
signature: Tells baroque stories of revenge and desire in meticulous, ornate images.
description: A former critic who studied philosophy. His films are ornate, perverse and exactingly designed, usually about revenge and its futility.

name: Vittorio De Sica
signature: An actor turned director who found heartbreak in the smallest stories of postwar poverty.
description: A matinee idol who directed with the screenwriter Cesare Zavattini. Their neorealist films find tragedy in a stolen bicycle or an old man's pension.

name: Luchino Visconti
signature: An aristocrat and Marxist who began in neorealism and ended in operatic period epics.
description: A Milanese aristocrat and Communist. His career ran from the proto-neorealism of Ossessione to sumptuous studies of aristocratic decline, staged with an opera director's eye.

name: Éric Rohmer
signature: Made talk the action: his characters explain themselves at length and then do something else.
description: The oldest of the New Wave critics. His films are comedies of self-deception in which educated people talk about love and then act against everything they said.

name: Wim Wenders
signature: The poet of the road movie, fascinated by American landscapes and European rootlessness.
description: A leading figure of the New German Cinema, obsessed with American music and movies. His road films follow lonely men across landscapes, with Robby Müller's photography.

name: Francis Ford Coppola
signature: Made four landmark films in the 1970s and repeatedly gambled his fortune on personal visions.
description: The first of the film-school generation to succeed in Hollywood. In the 1970s he made four of the decade's defining films and spent the fortune they earned on his own studio.

name: Hou Hsiao-hsien
signature: Recalls Taiwan's past in distant, patient long takes where history happens at the edge of the frame.
description: The central director of the Taiwan New Wave. He films from a distance in long takes, letting history register in family life and off-screen events.

name: Edward Yang
signature: Mapped modern Taipei as a web of families, offices and reflections in glass.
description: A former computer engineer who became the chronicler of Taipei. His films are novelistic in scope, with many characters observed through windows and reflections.

name: Thomas Vinterberg
signature: Co-founded Dogme 95 and made its first and most celebrated film.
description: A Danish director who co-wrote the Dogme 95 rules at 26. His films set groups of people against a truth one of them insists on telling.

name: Jafar Panahi
signature: Keeps making films in defiance of an official ban, turning the restriction itself into his subject.
description: Started as Kiarostami's assistant. Officially banned from filmmaking since 2010, he has kept making films in secret, in his flat, in a taxi and near the border.

name: Věra Chytilová
signature: The most formally radical voice of the Czechoslovak New Wave, anarchic and feminist.
description: The first woman to study directing at the Prague film school. Her films are aggressive experiments in montage and colour that mock both consumerism and socialist propriety.

name: Miloš Forman
signature: Carried the comic eye of the Czechoslovak New Wave into Hollywood stories of rebels against institutions.
description: Made comedies with non-actors in Czechoslovakia before emigrating. His American films side with misfits against institutions, from the asylum to the imperial court.

name: Nagisa Oshima
signature: Attacked Japanese taboos on sex, crime and the state, changing style with every film.
description: The leader of the Japanese New Wave. He rejected the humanism of the older masters and attacked taboos around sex, crime and the treatment of Koreans in Japan.

name: Shohei Imamura
signature: Said he was interested in the lower part of the human body and the lower part of the social structure.
description: Ozu's former assistant, who reacted against his refinement. He filmed pimps, bar hostesses and peasants with an anthropologist's curiosity and earthy humour.

name: Lee Chang-dong
signature: A novelist turned director whose slow-burning dramas turn on grief, faith and class.
description: A novelist who turned to film in his forties. His slow, morally searching dramas follow people undone by grief or injustice.

name: Ken Loach
signature: Has spent six decades filming working-class Britain with documentary directness and open political anger.
description: Began in BBC television drama in the 1960s. His films are made with social workers' accuracy and often non-professional casts, and are open about their politics.

name: Mike Leigh
signature: Builds his scripts through months of improvisation with the actors before shooting a word.
description: Develops each film from nothing through months of improvisation with the cast. The results are precisely scripted tragicomedies of English class and family.

name: Charlie Chaplin
signature: Created the Tramp, the most recognised character of the silent era, and mixed slapstick with pathos.
description: Rose from London poverty to become the most famous man in the world. He controlled every part of his films and shot scenes over and over until the comedy was exact.

name: Buster Keaton
signature: The Great Stone Face, who did his own dangerous stunts and treated the film frame as a gag machine.
description: A vaudeville child performer who became the great engineer of silent comedy. His gags are filmed in long, wide shots so the audience can see they are real.

name: Howard Hawks
signature: Mastered almost every Hollywood genre with an invisible style, fast talk and codes of professionalism.
description: Made classics in almost every genre without drawing attention to his style. His films are about groups of professionals, and his women talk as fast as his men.

name: Billy Wilder
signature: A writer first, whose cynical wit ran from film noir to farce.
description: An Austrian journalist and screenwriter who fled to Hollywood. He always wrote with a partner and directed to protect the script, in dramas and comedies equally cynical about people.

name: Michael Powell and Emeric Pressburger
signature: A writer-director partnership, The Archers, who made British cinema's most extravagant colour fantasies.
description: The English director Powell and the Hungarian writer Pressburger shared every credit. Their wartime and postwar films are romantic, mystical and visually extravagant, against the realist grain of British cinema.

name: Pier Paolo Pasolini
signature: A poet and novelist who filmed the sacred and the scandalous with the same frontal simplicity.
description: A poet, novelist and polemicist before he directed. He filmed Roman slum life, the Gospel and medieval tales in a deliberately rough, frontal style he compared to early Renaissance painting.

name: Bernardo Bertolucci
signature: Combined political history, psychoanalysis and sweeping camera movement.
description: A poet's son who was Pasolini's assistant at twenty. His films link sexuality and politics, photographed by Vittorio Storaro in sweeping, colour-coded movements.

name: Claude Chabrol
signature: The New Wave's specialist in murder among the provincial bourgeoisie.
description: Made the first New Wave feature with an inheritance. He settled into a long series of thrillers that observe bourgeois families with amused detachment.

name: Jacques Rivette
signature: Made long, playful films about theatre, conspiracy and performance.
description: The most experimental of the Cahiers critics. His long films, often developed with the actors, imagine Paris as a web of rehearsals and conspiracies.

name: Chris Marker
signature: The great film essayist, who thought aloud about memory, travel and images.
description: A writer, photographer and traveller who avoided publicity. His essay films think aloud about memory, politics and images.

name: Jacques Demy
signature: Set bittersweet fairy tales in French port towns, in candy colours and often entirely in song.
description: Grew up in Nantes and set his films in French port towns. They look like confectionery and are about chance, absence and lost love.

name: Roman Polanski
signature: A specialist in paranoia and confinement, usually seen through one character's eyes.
description: Trained at the Łódź film school and worked in Poland, Britain, Hollywood and France. His films trap characters in rooms and in their own perceptions.

name: Krzysztof Kieślowski
signature: Moved from documentary to metaphysical dramas about chance, coincidence and moral choice.
description: A Polish documentarist who came to distrust documentary. His later films are moral fables about chance and connection, tightly designed around colour and music.

name: Theo Angelopoulos
signature: Staged Greek history as slow processions in mist, in takes that travel through time within a single shot.
description: A Greek director who told his country's twentieth-century history as myth. His very long takes glide through landscapes while decades pass within a single shot.

name: Cristian Mungiu
signature: A leading figure of the Romanian New Wave, known for tense scenes played out in unbroken takes.
description: A former journalist and teacher. His films set ordinary Romanians moral traps and watch them in long takes without music.

name: Cristi Puiu
signature: Set the template for the Romanian New Wave with long, darkly comic dramas that unfold in near real time.
description: A painter who started the Romanian New Wave. His films follow people through hospitals and family gatherings in near real time, with grim humour.

name: Brian De Palma
signature: A virtuoso of the set piece, devoted to split screens, long takes and Hitchcock.
description: Part of the film-school generation. He turns thrillers into exercises in pure cinema, with split screens, long tracking shots and open borrowings from Hitchcock.

name: Sam Peckinpah
signature: Changed screen violence with slow motion and rapid intercutting, in elegies for men out of their time.
description: A television western writer who became the genre's elegist. His films are about ageing men with outdated codes, and their violence is drawn out in slow motion.

name: Spike Lee
signature: A confrontational, stylish chronicler of Black American life and of New York.
description: Emerged from NYU and Brooklyn in the 1980s. His films are argumentative and stylised, mixing comedy, music and direct address to confront American racism.

name: Richard Linklater
signature: Fascinated by time passing and people talking, often over a single day.
description: A self-taught filmmaker from Austin, Texas. He is interested in ordinary time: single days, long conversations and actors ageing across years.

name: David Fincher
signature: A perfectionist of dark, precise thrillers, known for demanding dozens of takes.
description: Came from visual effects and music videos. His thrillers are controlled to the frame, digitally polished and bleak about institutions and obsession.

name: Christopher Nolan
signature: Makes large-scale films built on puzzles of time, favouring film stock and practical effects.
description: A British-American director who writes most of his own scripts. He builds blockbusters around fractured timelines and prefers film cameras and physical effects.

name: David Cronenberg
signature: The originator of body horror, who films mutation and desire with clinical calm.
description: A Canadian who began in low-budget horror. His films treat the body as the place where technology, disease and desire rewrite identity.

name: Zhang Yimou
signature: Began as a cinematographer and became China's great colourist.
description: Trained as a cinematographer in the first class after the Cultural Revolution. His early films used saturated colour to tell stories of oppressed women; later he turned to martial-arts spectacle.

name: Chen Kaige
signature: Launched the Fifth Generation and went on to large historical dramas.
description: A classmate of Zhang Yimou at the Beijing Film Academy. His debut announced a new Chinese cinema of landscape and silence, and he later made lavish historical dramas.

name: Jia Zhangke
signature: Records China's upheaval through the people it leaves behind, mixing staged and found reality.
description: The leading director of China's Sixth Generation. He films provincial towns and migrant workers as the country is rebuilt around them, mixing documentary and fiction.

name: Ousmane Sembène
signature: Often called the father of African cinema, a novelist who turned to film to reach a wider audience.
description: A Senegalese novelist who took up film to reach people who could not read. His films criticise colonialism, the new African elite and patriarchal custom.

name: Glauber Rocha
signature: The voice of Cinema Novo, who wanted a cinema as violent as the hunger it showed.
description: The theorist and leading director of Brazil's Cinema Novo. His films are delirious political allegories set in the drought-stricken backlands.

name: Jane Campion
signature: Films desire and repression from inside her characters, with landscapes that press in on them.
description: A New Zealander trained in Australia. Her films centre on women's desire and will, with a strong sense of landscape and touch.

name: Céline Sciamma
signature: Films girlhood, identity and the act of looking with restraint and precision.
description: A French writer-director whose films follow girls and women working out who they are. Her style is spare, with little music and careful attention to looks exchanged.

name: Lucrecia Martel
signature: Builds unease from sound and from what sits just outside the frame.
description: An Argentine director from the northern province of Salta. Her films build a sense of decay and menace from overlapping sound and partial views.

name: Yorgos Lanthimos
signature: Sets absurd rules for his characters and has them speak in flat, stilted lines.
description: Came out of Greek theatre, video and advertising. His films place characters in closed systems with arbitrary rules and observe them with clinical humour.

name: Nuri Bilge Ceylan
signature: A former photographer who films Anatolian landscapes and long, searching conversations.
description: A Turkish photographer turned director. His films are slow studies of pride and disappointment among provincial men, with long conversations and wide Anatolian landscapes.

name: Takeshi Kitano
signature: A television comedian who became a director of still, melancholy gangster films punctuated by sudden violence.
description: One of Japan's most famous comedians, who took over a film when its director fell ill. His crime films alternate long stillness with abrupt violence and childlike play.

name: Ernst Lubitsch
signature: Master of sophisticated comedy, famous for the Lubitsch touch: saying the scandalous thing by showing a closed door.
description: Came from Berlin to Hollywood in 1922 and set the standard for witty, adult comedy of manners. His films trust the audience to complete the joke, implying sex and deceit through objects, doors and reaction shots.

name: Woody Allen
signature: Turned the neurotic New York intellectual into a film genre of its own.
description: A stand-up and gag writer who has made close to a film a year since the 1970s, mixing romantic comedy with borrowings from Bergman and Fellini. Long master shots let his actors talk over and past each other.

name: David Lean
signature: Began with intimate British dramas and became the definition of the widescreen epic.
description: A former editor whose cutting is as famous as his vistas. From Brief Encounter to Lawrence of Arabia he kept private emotion at the centre of ever larger canvases.

name: Stanley Donen & Gene Kelly
signature: Took the musical out of the theatre and made dance something only a camera could capture.
description: The dancer-choreographer and the young director co-directed three MGM musicals. Their numbers are filmed in long, mobile takes that show the whole body, and Singin' in the Rain turns Hollywood's own conversion to sound into comedy.

name: Ridley Scott
signature: A designer of worlds, from the rain-soaked future of Blade Runner to ancient Rome.
description: Trained as a designer and made hundreds of commercials before turning to features. His films are remembered first for atmosphere: smoke, backlight and densely layered sets.

name: Jean Vigo
signature: Made under three hours of film before dying at 29, and changed French cinema anyway.
description: The son of an anarchist, he mixed documentary roughness with lyrical fantasy. Zero for Conduct, about a schoolboy revolt, and the barge romance L'Atalante were banned or mutilated on release and rediscovered after the war.

name: Max Ophüls
signature: The poet of the moving camera, gliding through ballrooms and up staircases after women in love.
description: A German-born director who worked in Germany, France, Hollywood and France again. His elaborate crane and dolly shots circle characters caught between desire and social ritual.

name: Michael Curtiz
signature: The Warner Bros. workhorse who could direct anything, and directed Casablanca.
description: A Hungarian émigré who made around a hundred Hollywood films in every genre. Fluid camera movement and bold shadows give even routine assignments visual drive.

name: John Huston
signature: A writer-director of adventures about people undone by their own schemes.
description: Began as a screenwriter and adapted literature throughout his career, from Hammett to Joyce. His stories of doomed quests are told plainly, with close attention to faces and group dynamics.

name: D.W. Griffith
signature: Consolidated the grammar of narrative film, and used it for one of cinema's most racist works.
description: Made hundreds of shorts at Biograph, refining close-ups and parallel editing into a storytelling system. The Birth of a Nation glorified the Ku Klux Klan and provoked nationwide protest; Intolerance was his colossal reply to his critics.

name: Frank Capra
signature: Champion of the ordinary citizen against the powerful, in fast-talking populist fables.
description: An Italian immigrant who became Columbia's star director. His comedies move at speed but turn on a moment of despair before the community rallies round the hero.

name: Hayao Miyazaki
signature: Hand-draws worlds of flight, forests and spirits, and children who meet them without fear.
description: Co-founder of Studio Ghibli, where he storyboards his films himself and lets the story emerge as he draws. His films avoid clear villains and leave room for quiet pauses.

name: Nicholas Ray
signature: The poet of outsiders and troubled youth in 1950s Hollywood.
description: His characters are lonely, violent and tender, framed in bold colour and off-balance CinemaScope compositions. The French New Wave critics treated him as proof that a studio director could be an artist.

name: Vincente Minnelli
signature: MGM's great stylist, who treated colour and decor as the emotions of his characters.
description: A former stage designer who made the studio's most elegant musicals and some of its most intense melodramas. His crane shots sweep through crowded, colour-coded sets.

name: Carol Reed
signature: Made postwar Europe look tilted and treacherous.
description: A British craftsman whose late-1940s thrillers use real ruined cities, steep shadows and canted framing. Several of his stories are seen through the eyes of a child or an innocent out of his depth.

name: Leo McCarey
signature: Moved between anarchic comedy and tearjerkers, often improvising on set.
description: Learned his craft directing Laurel and Hardy shorts. He worked loosely, sometimes inventing scenes at a piano on the set, and let the actors' timing set the rhythm.

name: Victor Fleming
signature: The studio fixer credited with both of 1939's most famous films.
description: A former cameraman and reliable MGM professional who took over The Wizard of Oz and Gone with the Wind from other directors. He is remembered less for a personal style than for bringing huge productions home.

name: Preston Sturges
signature: Wrote and directed a burst of the fastest, wittiest American comedies within five years.
description: The first major Hollywood screenwriter of the sound era to direct his own scripts. His films combine sophisticated verbal comedy with pratfalls and a stock company of character actors.

name: Elia Kazan
signature: Brought Method acting from the stage to the screen.
description: Co-founder of the Actors Studio, he drew raw, psychologically detailed performances from Marlon Brando and James Dean. He pushed Hollywood toward location shooting and social subjects.

name: Marcel Carné
signature: Defined French poetic realism: doomed lovers in foggy, studio-built streets.
description: Worked with the poet Jacques Prévert as screenwriter and the designer Alexandre Trauner. Their films of the late 1930s set fatalistic romances in meticulously constructed sets.

name: Nicolas Roeg
signature: Shattered chronology so that past, present and premonition play at once.
description: A leading cinematographer before he directed. His editing associates images across time, so a scene can be interrupted by what will happen or what is remembered.

name: Gillo Pontecorvo
signature: Made a staged film about colonial war look like captured newsreel.
description: A former partisan and journalist who made only five features. The Battle of Algiers restaged the Algerian uprising on the real streets with a cast made up almost entirely of non-professionals.

name: Erich von Stroheim
signature: Hollywood's first great realist and its first great casualty of the studio system.
description: An Austrian émigré who invented an aristocratic past for himself. His obsessive detail and adult cynicism led to huge budgets and battles with producers, and most of his films survive only in cut versions.

name: Víctor Erice
signature: Made four features in fifty years, each a hushed study of memory and looking.
description: His films approach the silence of Spain after the civil war through children and through light falling into rooms. He works so rarely that each film is an event.

name: Claude Lanzmann
signature: Told the story of the Holocaust without a single frame of archive footage.
description: A journalist and editor of Les Temps modernes. Shoah, more than nine hours long, consists only of present-day testimony from survivors, bystanders and perpetrators, and of the sites as they look now.

name: Josef von Sternberg
signature: Painted with light and shadow, and made Marlene Dietrich a myth.
description: He treated story as a pretext for texture: veils, nets, smoke and shafts of light fill every layer of the frame. His films with Dietrich are studies in desire and humiliation.

name: Jacques Tourneur
signature: Frightened audiences with what he did not show.
description: The son of the silent director Maurice Tourneur. In low-budget horror for the producer Val Lewton, and later in film noir, he creates threat through shadow, sound and suggestion.

name: Joseph L. Mankiewicz
signature: Hollywood's most literate writer-director, who built films out of talk and flashbacks.
description: His films are witty, word-driven studies of ambition, theatre people and marriage, often told by several narrators in turn.

name: Sidney Lumet
signature: The great director of New York, juries, cops and institutions under pressure.
description: Came from live television and worked fast, with long rehearsals and few takes. His films test individuals against corrupt or indifferent systems.

name: Jean Eustache
signature: Made the definitive film about the hangover after May 1968.
description: A disciple of the New Wave who pushed its talkiness to an extreme. The Mother and the Whore is more than three and a half hours of confession, seduction and monologue in cafés and bedrooms.

name: John Carpenter
signature: Made lean genre films in widescreen, and usually wrote the synthesizer score himself.
description: A devotee of Howard Hawks who applied classical craft to horror and science fiction on small budgets. His films trap small groups with a threat they barely understand.

name: James Cameron
signature: Pushes film technology forward with every blockbuster.
description: A former truck driver and effects technician who writes his own scripts. His films combine engineering ambition with tightly constructed action.

name: Clint Eastwood
signature: The western's last star became its most reflective director.
description: Works quickly and economically, with few takes and low-key lighting. As a director he keeps returning to violence and what it costs the people who use it.

name: George Cukor
signature: The actor's director of classical Hollywood, with an unobtrusive camera.
description: Came from Broadway and let performance and dialogue lead. His comedies and literary adaptations are known above all for their female roles.

name: William Wyler
signature: The perfectionist of deep-focus staging, feared for demanding dozens of takes.
description: Used long takes staged in depth, so that the viewer chooses where to look, a style the critic André Bazin championed. His dramas are built on performance and moral pressure.

name: King Vidor
signature: Moved from silent social epics to fevered Technicolor melodrama.
description: His career ran from 1913 to 1959. The Crowd follows an ordinary clerk lost in the mass of the modern city, and his later films push emotion and landscape to extremes.

name: Michael Cimino
signature: Won everything with The Deer Hunter, then made the film blamed for ending New Hollywood.
description: His films stage long communal rituals, weddings, dances and hunts, before violence breaks in. His perfectionism on Heaven's Gate became a cautionary tale.

name: Jean-Marie Straub & Danièle Huillet
signature: The most uncompromising filmmakers in Europe: texts recited in landscapes, recorded in direct sound.
description: A couple who worked together for five decades. They film existing texts and music with fixed shots, non-professional readers and no dubbing, refusing every form of illusion.

name: Elem Klimov
signature: Made what many consider the most harrowing war film ever, then never directed again.
description: Come and See follows a boy through the Nazi destruction of Belarusian villages, with a roaming Steadicam and faces staring into the lens.

name: Robert Zemeckis
signature: A showman who hides ground-breaking effects inside crowd-pleasing stories.
description: A protégé of Steven Spielberg whose films are often built around a technical challenge, from mixing animation with live action to performance capture.

name: William Friedkin
signature: Brought documentary grit to the thriller and the horror film.
description: Began in television documentary and kept its handheld immediacy. His 1970s films treat police work and demonic possession with the same unblinking realism.

name: George Lucas
signature: Created Star Wars and, with it, the modern effects and franchise industry.
description: Started with experimental student films. His interest in sound, editing and myth produced Star Wars, and the companies he founded changed how films are made.

name: Stan Brakhage
signature: Made cinema a way of seeing, painting and scratching directly onto the film strip.
description: The central figure of American avant-garde film. His mostly silent films abandon story for rhythm, light and texture.

name: Mikio Naruse
signature: The bleakest of Japan's studio masters, chronicling women who keep going without hope.
description: His films are quiet dramas about money, work and disappointment, edited with unusual briskness. He is often named alongside Ozu, Mizoguchi and Kurosawa as the fourth master of classical Japanese cinema.

name: Sergei Parajanov
signature: Composed films as living icons and folk tapestries.
description: An Armenian born in Georgia who worked in Ukraine. After Shadows of Forgotten Ancestors he abandoned realism for frontal tableaux of costume, ritual and objects.

name: Michael Mann
signature: The stylist of professional men, night cities and cool blue light.
description: His crime films study experts at work, cops and thieves who mirror each other. He researches procedures in detail and shoots cities at night as glowing abstractions.

name: Maurice Pialat
signature: The harshest realist of French cinema, who cut scenes off before they resolved.
description: A painter who came late to film. He provoked his actors toward unguarded moments and edited around the raw result, leaving gaps where other films explain.

name: Michael Snow
signature: Made the camera's own movements the subject of his films.
description: A Canadian painter, sculptor and musician. His structural films each explore one camera operation, a zoom, a pan, a rotation, pushed to its limit.

name: Bob Fosse
signature: A choreographer who cut film the way he staged dance: sharp, angular and cynical.
description: He reinvented the film musical for a disillusioned era by confining the numbers to the stage and cutting them against the story.

name: Charles Burnett
signature: Filmed Black working-class life in Los Angeles with a tenderness American cinema had not shown it.
description: Part of the group of UCLA film students later called the L.A. Rebellion. Killer of Sheep observes a slaughterhouse worker and his neighbourhood in loose, plotless episodes.

name: Hal Ashby
signature: The gentle counterculture voice of 1970s Hollywood.
description: A former editor who made seven films in the 1970s about misfits and dropouts. His style is relaxed and observational, carried by pop songs.

name: Peter Weir
signature: Makes films about outsiders entering closed worlds, with an undertow of mystery.
description: A leading figure of the Australian New Wave who moved to Hollywood in the 1980s. His films set a rational outsider against a community or landscape that cannot be explained.

name: Rob Reiner
signature: Had a run of beloved films in a different genre each time.
description: An actor turned director whose 1980s films range from mock documentary to fairy tale, courtroom drama and romantic comedy.

name: Djibril Diop Mambéty
signature: Brought the freewheeling energy of the New Wave to Dakar.
description: A self-taught Senegalese filmmaker. His films are fragmented, musical and satirical, far from the social realism of his contemporaries.

name: Terry Gilliam
signature: Builds cluttered dystopias and fantasies seen through distorting wide lenses.
description: The American member of Monty Python. His films pit dreamers against bureaucracies, and his productions are famous for their disasters.

name: Andrzej Wajda
signature: The conscience of Polish cinema across fifty years of censorship and upheaval.
description: His early war trilogy founded the Polish Film School. He kept returning to moments when Polish history forced individuals to choose.

name: Todd Haynes
signature: Reworks old Hollywood forms, especially the women's picture, to ask what they concealed.
description: A leading figure of the New Queer Cinema of the early 1990s. His films borrow the look of earlier eras with scholarly precision.

name: Raoul Walsh
signature: The action director of classical Hollywood, all speed and outdoor energy.
description: Directed from the 1910s to the 1960s. His gangster films, westerns and war films move fast and stay close to physical action.

name: Jean Cocteau
signature: A poet who used simple camera tricks to film myths and dreams.
description: Poet, novelist, playwright and painter as well as filmmaker. His films make the fantastic matter-of-fact, with reversed motion and mirrors that turn to liquid.

name: Alexander Dovzhenko
signature: The lyric poet of Soviet cinema, rooted in the Ukrainian countryside.
description: Where Eisenstein's montage argues, his contemplates: fields, apples, faces and death held in still, hymn-like images.

name: Mike Nichols
signature: Came from improv comedy and gave 1960s Hollywood a new, anxious tone.
description: A Broadway director before his first film. He drew sharp comic performances and framed them in long, carefully composed takes.

name: George A. Romero
signature: Invented the modern zombie film and used it as social satire.
description: Worked outside Hollywood in Pittsburgh. Each of his Dead films uses the same premise to attack a different target, from racism to consumerism.

name: Abel Gance
signature: The most technically audacious director of the silent era.
description: His epics use rapid cutting, superimposition and a camera freed from the tripod years before these became common.

name: Ang Lee
signature: Moves between languages, genres and technologies, always circling repressed feeling.
description: Born in Taiwan and trained in the United States. He has made family comedies, Jane Austen, a martial-arts epic, a western romance and effects-driven spectacles.

name: Otto Preminger
signature: Used long, mobile takes to stay neutral and let the audience judge.
description: A Viennese stage director turned Hollywood producer-director. His films present institutions and trials from all sides without telling the viewer what to think.

name: Robert Aldrich
signature: Made brutal, cynical genre films shot from skewed angles.
description: An independent-minded director of war films, westerns and thrillers whose heroes are often as ugly as their enemies.

name: Tobe Hooper
signature: Made one of the most frightening films ever on a shoestring in the Texas heat.
description: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre feels like found evidence: grainy 16mm, relentless noise and almost no relief.

name: Robert J. Flaherty
signature: Often called the father of the documentary, though he staged much of what he filmed.
description: An explorer who lived with his subjects for long periods and filmed their struggle with nature as romantic drama.

name: Alfonso Cuarón
signature: Known for immersive long takes that follow characters through chaos.
description: A Mexican director who moves between Hollywood spectacle and personal films. His camera roams continuously, taking in the background as much as the leads.

name: Luis García Berlanga
signature: Smuggled savage satire past Franco's censors in crowded long takes.
description: His comedies fill the frame with people talking at once while the camera weaves between them. Under the jokes they are bleak portraits of Spanish society.

name: Mikhail Kalatozov
signature: Sent the camera flying through crowds, up stairwells and across rooftops.
description: A Georgian-born director whose films with the cinematographer Sergei Urusevsky are among the most acrobatic ever shot.

name: Gus Van Sant
signature: Alternates between studio films and minimalist experiments that follow young people on foot.
description: Based in Portland, Oregon. His most personal films trail drifters and teenagers in long walking shots and refuse to explain them.

name: Frederick Wiseman
signature: Has documented institutions for almost sixty years without narration or interviews.
description: Each film observes one institution, a hospital, a school, a welfare office, and finds its structure in the editing.

name: Andy Warhol
signature: Turned on the camera and let time and his superstars do the rest.
description: The pop artist made hundreds of films at his Factory in the 1960s, many of them single unedited reels of people sleeping, eating or talking.

name: Manoel de Oliveira
signature: Made films from the silent era until he was over a hundred.
description: The Portuguese director's late films are stately, literary and theatrical, filmed in fixed shots where actors speak the text out toward the audience.

name: Terence Davies
signature: Turned his Liverpool childhood into slow tracking shots and communal singing.
description: His autobiographical films are organised by memory instead of plot: songs, radio voices and tableaux of family life that dissolve into each other.

name: Peter Bogdanovich
signature: A critic who became a director to keep classical Hollywood alive.
description: He interviewed the old masters before directing films in their manner, in deep-focus black and white or as screwball comedy.

name: Maya Deren
signature: Founded the American avant-garde film with a fourteen-minute dream.
description: A dancer, theorist and organiser as well as a filmmaker. Her films cut between places on a single movement and loop events like a recurring dream.

name: George Miller
signature: Stages vehicular action as pure visual storytelling.
description: An Australian doctor turned director. The Mad Max films are chases told almost without dialogue, cut fast but composed so the eye never loses its place.

name: Pedro Costa
signature: Films Lisbon's poorest immigrants as if painting by candlelight.
description: Since the late 1990s he has worked with the residents of a demolished Lisbon slum, filming their stories in long, dark, carefully lit fixed shots.

name: Henri-Georges Clouzot
signature: France's master of suspense and misanthropy.
description: His thrillers are meticulously planned and pitiless about human motives. Le Corbeau, made during the occupation, got him banned from filmmaking for a time after the liberation.

name: Aleksandr Sokurov
signature: Tarkovsky's protégé, who bends and tints the image like an old painting.
description: A Russian director of elegies and portraits of power. He distorts the picture with lenses and filters until it resembles tarnished paint.

name: Ritwik Ghatak
signature: Made the Partition of Bengal the wound at the centre of all his films.
description: A Bengali contemporary of Satyajit Ray with the opposite temperament: operatic, jagged and angry, using melodrama and startling sound.

name: Samuel Fuller
signature: A tabloid reporter and infantryman who made films like front-page headlines.
description: He wrote, produced and directed low-budget war films, westerns and crime stories that hit taboo subjects head on.

name: Paul Verhoeven
signature: A Dutch provocateur who hid satire inside violent Hollywood blockbusters.
description: After a controversial career in the Netherlands he made American science fiction and thrillers that push sex and violence until they become commentary.

name: Emir Kusturica
signature: Fills the frame with brass bands, animals and chaos.
description: A Sarajevo-born director whose films treat Yugoslav history as a carnival, somewhere between Fellini and a wedding party out of control.

name: Louis Malle
signature: The New Wave's restless outsider, who never made the same kind of film twice.
description: He moved between thrillers, documentaries, scandal and autobiography, and between France and the United States.

name: John Boorman
signature: Drawn to myth, quests and men tested by the wilderness.
description: A British director who has worked on both sides of the Atlantic. His films push genre stories toward legend.

name: Robert Wise
signature: A former editor who worked expertly in every genre.
description: He directed horror, noir, science fiction and two of the most successful musicals ever made, adapting his style to each.

name: Arthur Penn
signature: Opened the door to New Hollywood with the gunfire that ends Bonnie and Clyde.
description: Came from live television and Broadway. He brought French New Wave abruptness to American genres.

name: Alexander Mackendrick
signature: Made Ealing's darkest comedies, then Hollywood's most acid film about power.
description: A Scottish-American director whose comedies have a streak of cruelty unusual for Ealing Studios.

name: Victor Sjöström
signature: The father of Swedish cinema, who made nature an actor.
description: His silent films use real landscapes and weather as moral forces, a decade before this was common.

name: Leos Carax
signature: The romantic wild child of French cinema.
description: He appeared in the 1980s as a prodigy steeped in silent film and Godard. His few films are extravagant, lovesick and full of sudden bursts of movement.

name: George Stevens
signature: Moved from light comedy to monumental American dramas after the war.
description: A former cameraman who shot Laurel and Hardy. After the war his films became slower, graver and more deliberate.

name: Marguerite Duras
signature: A novelist who separated voices from images.
description: One of France's major writers, she directed films in which what we hear and what we see drift apart.

name: Merian C. Cooper & Ernest B. Schoedsack
signature: Two adventurer-documentarists who invented the monster movie.
description: They filmed expeditions in Persia and Siam before turning their own exploits into the story of a film crew that brings back a giant ape.

name: Ermanno Olmi
signature: Carried neorealism on quietly for decades, with real workers and peasants.
description: Started by making documentaries for an electricity company. His features observe work and ritual with patience and gentle humour.

name: Lana Wachowski & Lilly Wachowski
signature: Fused Hong Kong action, anime and philosophy into The Matrix.
description: Sisters who write and direct together. Their films are maximalist, sincere and built from many sources at once.

name: G.W. Pabst
signature: The realist of Weimar cinema.
description: Associated with the New Objectivity that followed Expressionism. He was praised for psychological realism and for editing so smooth that cuts pass unnoticed.

name: Fei Mu
signature: Made what is often voted the greatest Chinese film.
description: A Shanghai director of the 1930s and 1940s. Spring in a Small Town is a restrained triangle among ruins, narrated by the wife.

name: Joseph Losey
signature: A blacklisted American who dissected the English class system.
description: After leaving Hollywood he rebuilt his career in Britain, where his films turn houses into arenas of class and sexual power.

name: Lynne Ramsay
signature: Tells stories through texture, sound and fragments instead of dialogue.
description: A Glasgow-born director who trained as a photographer. Her films stay inside damaged characters and show us details in place of explanations.

name: Jonathan Demme
signature: A humanist with a habit of having actors look straight into the lens.
description: Started with Roger Corman and moved between comedies, thrillers, documentaries and concert films with the same generosity toward his characters.

name: James Whale
signature: Gave Universal's monsters wit, pathos and Expressionist shadows.
description: An English stage director who made four classic horror films in the early 1930s, each laced with sly humour.

name: Barry Jenkins
signature: Films Black intimacy in saturated colour, with faces looking straight at us.
description: His films are tender, music-led studies of love and identity, shaped by Asian and European art cinema as much as by American tradition.

name: Tod Browning
signature: A former circus performer drawn to sideshows and outcasts.
description: His silent melodramas with Lon Chaney and his early sound films return again and again to the carnival and to bodies that society rejects.

name: Peter Jackson
signature: Went from splatter comedies to filming The Lord of the Rings in his native New Zealand.
description: A self-taught filmmaker who built an effects industry in Wellington to realise his projects.

name: Tim Burton
signature: Makes gothic fairy tales about gentle misfits.
description: A former Disney animator whose design-led films draw on German Expressionism, 1950s monster movies and suburbia.

name: Jonas Mekas
signature: The godfather of American avant-garde cinema and its tireless diarist.
description: A Lithuanian refugee who arrived in New York in 1949. He filmed his daily life in brief bursts for seven decades and edited the footage into long diary films.

name: Larisa Shepitko
signature: Made stark moral dramas before dying at 41.
description: A Ukrainian-born director whose films test individual conscience in extreme conditions, shot in harsh black and white.

name: Dario Argento
signature: The maestro of the Italian giallo, with murders staged like opera in primary colours.
description: His thrillers and supernatural horror films care less about logic than about colour, architecture, music and the killer's point of view.

name: Sofia Coppola
signature: Films privileged boredom and loneliness from the inside.
description: Her films are mood pieces about young women in gilded isolation, built on atmosphere and music more than plot.

name: John Schlesinger
signature: Moved from the British New Wave to a jagged portrait of New York.
description: Began in BBC documentaries. His 1960s films follow restless young people in a changing Britain.

name: Guru Dutt
signature: The melancholy poet of Hindi cinema's golden age.
description: Actor, producer and director. His films use song sequences, sweeping crane shots and deep shadows to tell stories of artists rejected by the world.

name: Michel Gondry
signature: A music-video inventor who prefers handmade, in-camera tricks.
description: A French director who brought the playful illusions of his videos into features about memory and dreams.

name: Frank Borzage
signature: Hollywood's great romantic, for whom love overcomes poverty and war.
description: His couples are poor, threatened and transfigured by devotion, filmed in soft light on stylised studio sets.

name: Alan J. Pakula
signature: The director of 1970s paranoia.
description: His thrillers dwarf their characters in dark, wide, architectural frames, suggesting forces they cannot see.

name: Tomás Gutiérrez Alea
signature: Cuba's leading filmmaker, loyal to the revolution and critical of it.
description: His films examine life after the revolution with irony, mixing fiction with documentary material.

name: King Hu
signature: Turned the martial arts film into visual poetry.
description: Working in Hong Kong and Taiwan, he drew on Peking opera for the rhythm of his fight scenes and on landscape painting for his compositions.

name: Anthony Mann
signature: Made westerns in which the landscape mirrors tormented heroes.
description: He moved from shadowy low-budget noirs to psychologically harsh westerns and then to epics.

name: Roy Andersson
signature: Builds each scene as one fixed, pale tableau of human absurdity.
description: A Swedish director whose late films are chains of vignettes, each a single deep-focus shot on a hand-built set with chalk-faced actors.

name: Kathryn Bigelow
signature: Makes action films about addiction to danger.
description: Trained as a painter. Her films put the viewer inside physical risk with restless, subjective camerawork.

name: Georges Franju
signature: Found poetry in horror and horror in the everyday.
description: He moved from unsettling documentaries to dreamlike thrillers that pay homage to silent serials.

name: Jacques Becker
signature: A craftsman of gestures, friendship and work.
description: His films attend to how people do things: cook, dress, dig a tunnel. The New Wave critics admired him as a model of precise, unpretentious craft.

name: Louis Feuillade
signature: The king of the crime serial.
description: As head of production at Gaumont he made hundreds of films. His serials stage wild plots in real Paris streets, in calm deep-focus long shots.

name: Hong Sang-soo
signature: Makes film after film about awkward drinking sessions, with a sudden zoom as his signature.
description: A prolific South Korean director of small, playful films in which stories repeat with variations.

name: Lindsay Anderson
signature: The angriest voice of the British New Wave.
description: A critic and documentarist before his first feature. His films attack British institutions with a mix of realism and Brechtian fantasy.

name: Errol Morris
signature: Has his subjects look straight into the lens and re-enacts their stories in stylised detail.
description: His documentaries are investigations into self-deception, combining interviews with re-enactments and a driving score.

name: Julie Dash
signature: Told Black women's history in a lyrical, non-linear style.
description: A member of the L.A. Rebellion. Daughters of the Dust portrays a Gullah family in 1902 through ritual, memory and landscape.

name: Francesco Rosi
signature: Invented the film investigation into power, crime and the Italian state.
description: His films reconstruct real cases as open inquiries, leaving the questions unanswered because the facts are.

name: Fred Zinnemann
signature: A realist of individual conscience.
description: A Viennese émigré trained in documentary. His films place one person's principles against a community's cowardice.

name: René Clair
signature: Brought the lightness of silent comedy into the sound era.
description: He came out of the Paris avant-garde and made some of the first inventive sound films, treating music and noise as comedy.

name: Raúl Ruiz
signature: A Chilean exile who made over a hundred labyrinthine films.
description: His stories branch, loop and contradict themselves, with a playful love of puzzles, ghosts and tall tales.

name: Giuseppe Tornatore
signature: Italian cinema's nostalgist.
description: A Sicilian director of sweeping, sentimental films about memory and the pull of home.

name: Jean Rouch
signature: An anthropologist who invented cinéma vérité and inspired the New Wave.
description: He made most of his films in West Africa, improvising stories together with the people he filmed.

name: Sydney Pollack
signature: A reliable maker of star-driven Hollywood dramas and comedies.
description: A former actor and acting teacher, valued by stars for the performances he drew from them.

name: Boris Barnet
signature: The lightest touch in Soviet cinema.
description: A pupil of Lev Kuleshov who preferred comedy, feeling and everyday detail to political argument.

name: John Waters
signature: Baltimore's Pope of Trash.
description: He made deliberately shocking underground comedies with a troupe of friends and later brought the same sensibility to the mainstream.

name: Robert Hamer
signature: Made the most elegant and poisonous of the Ealing comedies.
description: A former editor. Kind Hearts and Coronets tells of serial murder in the politest possible voice-over.

name: Don Siegel
signature: An economical action director.
description: He made tight, unsentimental thrillers about loners and institutions, mostly on modest budgets.

name: Robert Wiene
signature: Directed the film that defined Expressionism.
description: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari projects a madman's vision onto the world, with painted shadows and jagged, tilted sets.

name: Aleksei German
signature: Plunged the camera into crowded, chaotic recreations of Soviet history.
description: He made only six features. They are dense with overlapping talk and passing figures who glance at the lens.

name: David Hand
signature: Supervising director of Disney's first features.
description: He coordinated the teams of sequence directors and animators on Snow White and Bambi, under Walt Disney's close control.

name: Harold Ramis
signature: A comedy writer-director from Chicago's Second City.
description: He wrote and directed some of the defining American comedies of the 1980s and 1990s.

name: Mel Brooks
signature: The master of film parody.
description: A television gag writer who made spoofs of the western, the horror film and the Hitchcock thriller, breaking the fourth wall at will.

name: Derek Jarman
signature: Painter, activist and the leading figure of British queer cinema.
description: He made low-budget films mixing Super 8 footage, tableaux and anachronism.

name: Guillermo del Toro
signature: Makes fairy tales in which the monsters are more humane than the people.
description: A Mexican director who began as a make-up effects artist. His films are designed down to the last gear and creature.

name: Jordan Peele
signature: Uses horror to expose American racism.
description: He came from sketch comedy and writes his own tightly constructed, allegorical scripts.

name: Peter Watkins
signature: Stages history and future catastrophes as if television news crews were present.
description: A British director who has worked mostly in exile. His films use amateur casts and interview formats to attack the conventions of mass media.

name: Oliver Stone
signature: Makes aggressive, densely edited films about American power.
description: A Vietnam veteran who writes his own scripts. His films argue with recent American history, mixing film stocks and formats.

name: Charles Laughton
signature: A great actor who directed one film, a nightmare fairy tale like nothing else in Hollywood.
description: The Night of the Hunter combines silent-film lighting, storybook sets and a child's view of evil.

name: Barbara Loden
signature: Wrote, directed and starred in Wanda, a founding film of American independent cinema.
description: An actress who made one feature, about a woman who drifts away from her life in the Pennsylvania coal country.

name: Forugh Farrokhzad
signature: One of Iran's great modern poets, whose single short film seeded the Iranian New Wave.
description: The House Is Black sets her own verse and passages of scripture against images of daily life in a leprosy colony.

name: Fernando Meirelles
signature: Brought a kinetic, advertising-honed style to the favelas of Rio.
description: A Brazilian director who came from television and commercials.

name: Asghar Farhadi
signature: Builds moral thrillers out of domestic disputes in which everyone has their reasons.
description: His scripts turn on a small lie or an unseen event and let class, religion and pride do the rest.

name: Sara Maldoror
signature: A pioneer of African cinema, who filmed the liberation struggles of Portuguese-speaking Africa.
description: Born in France to a Guadeloupean father. Her films approach the independence wars through the daily lives of women.

name: Wang Bing
signature: Documents the people left behind by China's economic transformation at monumental length.
description: He usually works alone with a small digital camera, staying with factory workers, migrants and survivors of labour camps for months or years.

name: Med Hondo
signature: A Mauritanian-born filmmaker in France who attacked colonialism with Brechtian invention.
description: His films mix theatre, song, documentary and satire to tell the history of slavery, colonisation and immigration.

name: Cheryl Dunye
signature: Blends documentary and fiction, a mix she calls the Dunyementary.
description: She plays a version of herself in her films, talking to the camera about history, desire and who gets remembered.

name: Jennie Livingston
signature: Made the defining document of New York's ballroom culture.
description: Paris Is Burning records the drag balls of Harlem and the houses that compete in them.

name: Monte Hellman
signature: The minimalist of the American road movie and western.
description: He started out with Roger Corman. His films strip genre down to waiting, driving and silence.

name: Jonathan Glazer
signature: Makes about a film a decade, each a formal experiment.
description: He came from music videos and commercials. His features take a single unsettling idea and follow it with cold rigour.

name: Fernando E. Solanas
signature: Co-author of the Third Cinema manifesto.
description: An Argentine filmmaker and later politician. With Octavio Getino he called for a militant cinema that is neither Hollywood nor European art film.

name: Hiroshi Teshigahara
signature: Made existential allegories with the novelist Kōbō Abe and the composer Tōru Takemitsu.
description: Their films turn skin, sand and insects into abstract textures while their heroes lose their identities.

name: William Greaves
signature: Made a film about making a film about making a film.
description: A documentary producer and a pioneer of Black filmmaking on American public television.

name: Sally Potter
signature: Came to film from dance and performance art.
description: A British director and composer whose films question gender and storytelling conventions.

name: Isao Takahata
signature: The realist of Studio Ghibli.
description: Miyazaki's mentor and partner. He used animation for stories of ordinary life and loss, changing visual style with each film.

name: Joshua Oppenheimer
signature: Asked Indonesian death-squad veterans to re-enact their killings as movie scenes.
description: The Act of Killing lets the perpetrators of the 1965 massacres stage their memories in the style of their favourite films.

name: Andrzej Żuławski
signature: Films emotional extremes with a camera that never stops moving and actors pushed to hysteria.
description: A Polish director who worked largely in France after trouble with the censors at home.

name: Sara Gómez
signature: Cuba's first woman feature director.
description: She made documentaries about race, class and machismo in revolutionary Cuba before her only feature.

name: Patricio Guzmán
signature: Has spent fifty years recording Chile's memory.
description: After filming the fall of Allende he went into exile. His later films link the dictatorship's crimes to Chile's deserts, sea and mountains.

name: Elaine May
signature: A comic genius whose films bite harder than the studios wanted.
description: She let scenes run long and awkward, finding comedy in cruelty and self-deception.

name: Miklós Jancsó
signature: Choreographed history as ritual on the Hungarian plain.
description: Soldiers, prisoners and horsemen circle each other in endless tracking shots that turn power into abstract movement.

name: Masaki Kobayashi
signature: A pacifist who attacked authority and the samurai code.
description: His austere widescreen films show individuals crushed by military and feudal systems.

name: John Hughes
signature: Took teenagers seriously.
description: A former advertising copywriter who wrote and directed the defining American teen films of the 1980s.

name: John Landis
signature: Mixed anarchic comedy with other genres.
description: His films of the late 1970s and 1980s combine broad comedy with car chases, music and horror.

name: Albert Maysles & David Maysles
signature: Pioneers of direct cinema.
description: The brothers filmed with lightweight equipment and no interviews or narration, trusting what unfolded in front of them.

name: Blake Edwards
signature: Master of the slow-burn sight gag in wide frames.
description: He staged elaborate physical comedy in long, wide takes, letting disasters build in the background.

name: Leni Riefenstahl
signature: Put formal innovation at the service of Nazi propaganda.
description: A dancer and actress in mountain films before Hitler commissioned her to film the Nuremberg rally. Her work remains the central case in arguments about art and politics.

name: Edgar G. Ulmer
signature: Made stylish films from almost nothing on Hollywood's Poverty Row.
description: A designer in Weimar Germany who spent most of his American career at the cheapest studios.

name: Kira Muratova
signature: The most eccentric voice of Soviet and Ukrainian cinema.
description: She worked in Odessa. Her films are abrasive and funny, full of repetition and interruption.

name: Irvin Kershner
signature: The character director who made the darkest Star Wars film.
description: He came from documentary and television and was known for work with actors.

name: Cecil B. DeMille
signature: Hollywood's first showman, synonymous with the biblical epic.
description: Co-directed one of the first features shot in Hollywood and worked for five decades, mixing spectacle, piety and titillation. When Cannes commemorated its cancelled 1939 edition in 2002, a jury gave that year's prize to his Union Pacific.

name: Leopold Lindtberg
signature: A Vienna-born theatre director who made Swiss cinema's best-known films.
description: An exile from Austria who worked in Zurich. The Last Chance follows refugees crossing the Alps into Switzerland and was made while the war was still being fought.

name: Emilio Fernández
signature: El Indio, who gave Mexican cinema its heroic image of land and people.
description: With the cinematographer Gabriel Figueroa he created a monumental style of low horizons, vast skies and noble faces during the golden age of Mexican cinema.

name: František Čáp
signature: A Czech director whose resistance drama shared the first Cannes prize.
description: A prolific director of the 1940s who left Czechoslovakia after the Communist takeover and later worked in Slovenia.

name: Chetan Anand
signature: Made the first Indian film honoured at Cannes.
description: A founder of the Hindi film company Navketan with his brother Dev Anand. Neecha Nagar is a social allegory that drew on Soviet montage and expressionist lighting.

name: Jean Delannoy
signature: A pillar of the French tradition of quality that the New Wave attacked.
description: A polished director of literary adaptations and star vehicles across five decades.

name: Bodil Ipsen & Lau Lauritzen Jr.
signature: The Danish duo behind the first major films about the resistance.
description: Ipsen was one of Denmark's great stage actresses. With Lauritzen she co-directed thrillers and war dramas in the 1940s.

name: Alf Sjöberg
signature: Sweden's leading stage director, who won the top prize at Cannes twice.
description: Head director at Stockholm's Royal Dramatic Theatre. In Miss Julie, past and present share the same shot, an effect Bergman later developed.

name: Fridrikh Ermler
signature: A former secret-police agent who became a leading Soviet director.
description: Made psychologically acute silent films in Leningrad and later officially favoured dramas under Stalin.

name: Edward Dmytryk
signature: A noir stylist whose career was split by the blacklist.
